title: Recursive generics / self-bounded types: Enum<E extends Enum<E>>, fluent builders
shortTitle: What are recursive generics and self-bounded types?
keyPoints: Recursive generics (self-bounded types) is a pattern where the type parameter references the declaring class itself: class X<T extends X<T>>.
Java's Enum uses this pattern: Enum<E extends Enum<E>> ensures compareTo() only accepts the same enum type, not any Enum.
Fluent builder inheritance uses Builder<T extends Builder<T>> so that parent methods return the concrete builder subtype, not the abstract parent.
Without recursive generics, calling a parent builder method returns the parent type, breaking access to subclass-specific methods in the chain.
The unchecked cast return (T) this is typically needed in the abstract parent builder because the compiler cannot verify that this is T.
Comparable<T> uses a similar self-referential pattern: class Account implements Comparable<Account> restricts compareTo to Account only.
This pattern appears in Protocol Buffers builders, Lombok, Hibernate Criteria API, and many framework fluent APIs.

s1_definition.oneliner: Recursive generics (self-bounded types) is the pattern class X<T extends X<T>> where the type parameter references the declaring class, enabling type-safe fluent chains and self-referential methods like Enum's compareTo.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Self-bounded type** – `class Enum<E extends Enum<E>>` means E is bounded by Enum parameterised with E itself; this ensures compareTo accepts only the same concrete enum type
- **Fluent builder pattern** – `abstract class Builder<T extends Builder<T>>` lets parent methods return T (the concrete subclass), not the abstract Builder
- **The (T) this cast** – inside the abstract builder, `return (T) this` is needed because the compiler cannot verify that `this` is of type T; it is technically unchecked but safe by convention
- **Comparable** – `class Account implements Comparable<Account>` is a simpler form: compareTo accepts only Account, not any Object
- **Framework usage** – Protocol Buffers, Lombok @Builder with inheritance, Hibernate Criteria API, and Spring Security all use this pattern
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, recursive generics is like a form that says "the next form in this sequence must be the same type of form". A LoanApplication's follow-up field only accepts another LoanApplication, not a SavingsApplication. For builders, it is like a construction checklist where every step returns the specific checklist type. A HomeLoanBuilder.setInterestRate() returns HomeLoanBuilder, not generic Builder, so Rajesh can chain .setTenure() which only exists on HomeLoanBuilder.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Recursive Generics: Enum<E extends Enum<E>>
  =============================================

  abstract class Enum<E extends Enum<E>> implements Comparable<E> {
      public final int compareTo(E o) { ... }
  }

  enum TradeStatus { PENDING, SETTLED }
  -> class TradeStatus extends Enum<TradeStatus>
  -> compareTo(TradeStatus o)  // only accepts TradeStatus!

  enum AccountType { SAVINGS, CURRENT }
  -> class AccountType extends Enum<AccountType>
  -> compareTo(AccountType o)  // only accepts AccountType!

  TradeStatus.PENDING.compareTo(AccountType.SAVINGS)
  -> COMPILE ERROR! Types do not match.

  Fluent Builder Pattern:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ abstract class Builder<T extends Builder<T>> │
  │   T name(String n) { return (T) this; }  │
  │                                          │
  │ class HomeLoan extends Builder<HomeLoan>  │
  │   HomeLoan tenure(int y) { return this; } │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘

  new HomeLoan().name("Rajesh")  -> HomeLoan (not Builder!)
               .tenure(20)       -> HomeLoan (works!)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Recursive generics (self-bounded types) is the pattern where a type parameter is bounded by the declaring class itself. Java's Enum uses `Enum<E extends Enum<E>>` to ensure that compareTo only accepts the same enum type, preventing accidental comparison of TradeStatus with AccountType. The fluent builder pattern uses `Builder<T extends Builder<T>>` so that parent methods return the concrete subclass type, enabling unbroken method chaining.

Without this pattern, calling a parent builder method would return the abstract parent type, and subclass-specific methods would be inaccessible in the chain. The unchecked cast `(T) this` is safe by convention: subclasses pass themselves as T. An alternative is an abstract self() method that subclasses implement.

At National Bank of India, Pankaj designed the loan application builder using recursive generics. HomeLoanBuilder extended the base LoanBuilder, and methods like applicantName and amount (defined in the parent) returned HomeLoanBuilder, allowing Rajesh to chain .tenureYears() and .interestRate() without breaking the fluent API.

Remember one sentence: recursive generics like Enum<E extends Enum<E>> ensure type-safe self-referential methods, and Builder<T extends Builder<T>> ensures fluent chains return the concrete subclass type, not the abstract parent.
